headline: Nasdaq down 2.8% as AI-spending fears deepen; bitcoin near $81,300
summary: Heading into the last half-hour of trading, the Nasdaq is down about 2.8% and the S&P 500 about 1.4%, their weakest levels of the day, as Meta and AMD (each down about 8.3–8.5%) and Amazon (down about 5.3%) lead a tech and chip sell-off on doubts about the payoff from heavy AI spending. Bitcoin is steady near $81,300, down about 3.5% in a day, ether is near $2,385, and smaller coins such as LayerZero and Zcash are down roughly 10–11%, with total crypto value down about 6% to $2.74 trillion. The TSX is down about 0.9% as gold falls 2.5% and Shopify slides 4%, U.S. crude is near $99.50 on Middle East supply fears, and the 10-year Treasury yield has dropped to about 4.95% as investors buy bonds for safety.

crypto.label: Risk-off
crypto.why: Bitcoin is down about 3.5% and ether about 4.4% in 24 hours, most large altcoins are down 5–11%, and total crypto value is down about 6%, even though the daily Fear & Greed reading (68, Greed) has not yet caught up.

stocks.label: Risk-off
stocks.why: The Nasdaq is down about 2.8% and the S&P 500 about 1.4%, with Meta and AMD down more than 8%, Amazon over 5% and Nvidia over 4%, the VIX fear gauge up about 20% to near 20, and investors piling into Treasuries.

drivers.title: AI-spending doubts hit Big Tech and chips
drivers.detail: Meta is down about 8.3% to near $640 even after beating forecasts, as investors weigh its $135–$145 billion spending plan, negative free cash flow and a surprise new non-voting share class; AMD is down about 8.5%, Amazon about 5.3%, Nvidia and Broadcom about 4–4.5%, and Lam Research fell about 9% after its results. A report that Nvidia and Tesla plan to invest in a Samsung supplier revived worries about 'circular' AI deals, where chip buyers and sellers fund each other.
drivers.assets: Nasdaq, chip stocks, Shopify, Celestica, bitcoin

drivers.title: Stablecoin rules finalized
drivers.detail: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), a top U.S. bank regulator, finalized reserve, redemption and risk rules for stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act, taking effect in January 2027. Crypto stocks rallied on it Wednesday, but Coinbase and Strategy are giving back about 4.6% and 5.6% today with bitcoin.

drivers.title: Bond yields tumble as investors seek safety
drivers.detail: The 10-year Treasury yield has dropped to about 4.95% from 5.15%, on track for one of its biggest one-day falls in more than two years, as money leaves tech stocks for government bonds. Weekly jobless claims fell to 194,000, a sign the job market is still tight, so the Fed is still expected to hold at 3.75%–4.00% on Oct. 28 rather than cut.

drivers.title: Oil near $100 on Saudi attacks
drivers.detail: U.S. crude is up about 2.4% to roughly $99.50 a barrel and Brent near $112, its highest since May, after attacks on a Saudi airport and an Aramco oil field and a New York Times report that the U.S. and Israel have drawn up plans for renewed Iran strikes after the Nov. 3 midterms. Higher oil feeds inflation fears, while gold is down about 2.5% to near $4,045 and copper hit a five-week low, sinking Canadian miners.
drivers.assets: Oil, Canadian energy stocks, bonds, crypto

drivers.title: Bitcoin ETF buying is back, but modest
drivers.detail: Spot bitcoin ETFs (funds that hold real bitcoin) took in more than $1 billion over the first three days of this week, per SoSoValue data cited by CoinDesk, while ether funds have lost more than $1 billion this month. Even so, bitcoin has slid to about $81,000 with tech stocks, and about $431 million of leveraged bets were wiped out in the overnight drop.

drivers.title: Bank of Canada expected to hold
drivers.detail: Canadian headline inflation rose to 3.1% on gas prices, but core measures eased, and economists expect the Bank to hold at 2.25% on Oct. 28. Hopes for progress in Canada–U.S. trade talks helped the TSX to a four-week high Wednesday.

crypto.name: Bitcoin
crypto.move: Down 3.5% in 24h and 1.3% this week, to about $81,300 (down 6% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Bitcoin climbed to nearly $85,000 late Wednesday, briefly breaking above the $84,000 ceiling that had stopped it on Oct. 13–14, then fell back below $82,000 overnight as Tesla's and Meta's results revived doubts about AI spending; it has held near $81,000–$81,300 as the Nasdaq's losses deepened to more than 2%. The round trip caused about $431 million of liquidations (leveraged bets closed automatically), per CoinDesk. Bitcoin's share of total crypto value is near 59.5%, close to its highest since May, as traders shelter in it while smaller coins fall harder. Spot bitcoin ETFs still took in more than $1 billion over three days.
crypto.meaning: Bitcoin is now trading closely with tech stocks, and it is sitting just above the $80,000 floor of the $80,000–$87,000 range it has held for a month. ETF buying helps, but it is below the pace that came with past strong rallies, and some traders warn that a clean break below about $80,000 could open a slide toward $75,000 or lower.

outlook.bullCase: Reclaiming $84,000–$85,000 with steady ETF inflows and a firmer Nasdaq could carry it to the top of the range near $87,000–$87,500; a break above that would be a bigger shift.
outlook.bearCase: A further slide in tech stocks, a hawkish Fed on Oct. 28, or higher oil could push it below the $80,000 floor, with some traders eyeing $75,000–$70,000 if that gives way.
outlook.watch: Whether the Nasdaq steadies into the close, the $80,000 and $85,000 levels, daily ETF flows, and the Fed decision on Oct. 28.

crypto.name: Ethereum
crypto.move: Down 4.4% in 24h and 2.4% this week, to about $2,385 (down 13.5% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Ether briefly rose to about $2,490 with bitcoin on Wednesday, then gave the gain back and has now slipped below the $2,400 level that had held as support for about a week. It keeps trailing bitcoin as U.S. ether ETFs kept losing money: about $26 million on Tuesday and an estimated $31 million more on Wednesday, taking October outflows past $1 billion, the worst month of 2026. On the plus side, a record 43.8 million ETH (about 36% of supply) is staked, meaning locked up to secure the network.
crypto.meaning: Ether is lagging bitcoin because big investors keep pulling money from the ETFs. Until those flows turn, rallies may be harder to sustain.

outlook.bullCase: Reclaiming $2,400 quickly, ETF outflows stopping and a firm hold above $2,500 could open a move toward about $2,700, where October began.
outlook.bearCase: Staying below $2,400 with continued ETF outflows could send it toward the $2,300 area, and a broader risk-off turn could push it lower.
outlook.watch: Daily ether ETF flows, the $2,400 and $2,500 levels, and the ETH/BTC ratio.

crypto.name: LayerZero
crypto.move: Down 11.1% in 24h and 14.4% this week, to about $1.81 (up 27% over 30 days)
crypto.why: LayerZero, a service that lets apps pass messages and tokens between blockchains, is the biggest decliner in the top 100 today. No project-specific news (hack, outage or unlock) has been reported; analysts tie it to the broad sell-off in DeFi and smaller coins and heavy selling after a strong run, with the token up more than 100% over 90 days. It fell from about $2.03 to $1.76 with trading volume below its 30-day average, per DiarioBitcoin's analysis.
crypto.meaning: Tokens that ran up fast are being sold hardest as traders retreat to bitcoin. The planned launch of its Zero and lzATLAS products on Nov. 30 is the next project catalyst, but it does not offset today's market-wide selling, and ZRO is still about 76% below its December 2024 record.

outlook.bullCase: If altcoins stabilize, a recovery above about $1.87–$1.91 on rising volume could bring the $2.00 area back into view.
outlook.bearCase: If selling continues, the next support is near its 50-day average around $1.55.
outlook.watch: Bitcoin dominance (a falling share would signal money returning to altcoins), the $1.76 low, and news on the Nov. 30 product launch.

crypto.name: Zcash
crypto.move: Down 9.6% in 24h and about 1% this week, to about $1,218 (down 21% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Traders had been positioning for the NU7 upgrade, which developers scheduled for about 7:50 p.m. ET on Nov. 5; it cuts block times from 75 to 25 seconds and sends 60% of fees to a reserve. Futures open interest (the value of open bets) had risen about 19–24% and two large traders reportedly opened about $37.6 million of 10x leveraged longs. Today those leveraged bets are unwinding: CoinDesk flagged ZEC among the coins where bullish traders are closing positions, and the price has fallen about 11% to just above the $1,190–$1,230 support area.
crypto.meaning: Much of this month's rally was driven by borrowed money, and today shows how fast that can reverse. Upgrade dates often bring 'buy the rumour, sell the news' behaviour, so swings both ways are likely into Nov. 5.

outlook.bullCase: Holding the $1,180–$1,200 area and renewed interest as the upgrade nears could bring it back to the $1,375 resistance and, beyond that, the September high near $1,700.
outlook.bearCase: Losing $1,180 would erase the October breakout and could send it toward about $1,000–$1,120, near its 50-day average.
outlook.watch: The $1,180 level, funding rates and open interest, ETF flows, and any upgrade delay.

crypto.name: Ethena
crypto.move: Down 8.3% in 24h and 1.3% this week, to about $0.201 (down 3% over 30 days)
crypto.why: ENA led large-cap gainers on Wednesday, then reversed as DeFi tokens (decentralized-finance apps) led crypto lower: CoinDesk's DeFi index fell about 6% overnight and ENA is down about 8% on the day, roughly 25% below its late-September peak. The earlier rally looked driven by momentum, with the hourly RSI (a gauge of how overstretched a move is) hitting about 73, an overbought reading. A longer-term support is that the last tranche of early-investor tokens unlocked on Oct. 5, ending Ethena's monthly investor unlocks.
crypto.meaning: With the investor unlock overhang gone, ENA's supply picture is cleaner, but USDe, the synthetic dollar that drives Ethena's revenue, is far below its 2025 peak. A one-day pop on no clear news can unwind just as fast.

outlook.bullCase: A sustained move above about $0.2165, with USDe supply growing again, could carry ENA toward the mid-$0.20s.
outlook.bearCase: It is now testing about $0.195 (its 50-day average); a clear break below would erase this week's gains and could bring the mid-$0.18s into view.
outlook.watch: USDe supply, the $0.195–$0.2165 range, and broader altcoin risk appetite.

crypto.name: NEAR Protocol
crypto.move: Down 7.2% in 24h and 7.5% this week, to about $4.91 (up 10% over 30 days)
crypto.why: NEAR has been one of October's strongest large coins. Supports include the first U.S. spot NEAR ETF from Bitwise (launched Sept. 29), a governance proposal to cut yearly new-token issuance from 2.5% to 1.6%, and strong use of its NEAR Intents cross-chain swap service. It led the CoinDesk 100 on Wednesday without a fresh headline and is giving that back today, with CoinDesk noting open interest fell about 9% as leveraged buyers closed positions.
crypto.meaning: The rally has real drivers behind it, but the issuance cut is only a proposal and NEAR is already back near its early-October highs around $6. Fast multi-week runs tend to see sharp pullbacks.

outlook.bullCase: Approval of the issuance cut and continued ETF inflows could push NEAR back to test the $5.60–$6.00 area hit earlier this month.
outlook.bearCase: A further unwinding of leveraged bets, or the proposal stalling, could take it toward $4.50 or below; it has now slipped back under $5.
outlook.watch: The issuance-cut vote, NEAR ETF flows, and whether it can get back above $5.

crypto.name: Monero
crypto.move: About flat in 24h and up 11.8% this week, at about $610 (up 6% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Monero, a privacy-focused coin that hides who sends what, is one of the few large coins rising today, trading near $615 after briefly touching about $650 overnight. There is no project-specific news behind it: the latest software release on Oct. 16 was routine maintenance. The run started after veteran chart trader Peter Brandt called XMR his favourite large-cap setup, and futures trading volume has outpaced spot (actual coin) trading, a sign that leveraged bets are doing much of the lifting. Futures funding rates (the fee bullish leveraged traders pay to keep bets open) are running near 70% a year, far above other coins, per CoinDesk, which shows how crowded the bullish side is.
crypto.meaning: Rallies driven by borrowed money can reverse quickly if traders are forced to close positions (a liquidation). Monero is also still about 18% below its January record near $799, and an EU anti-money-laundering rule from July 2027 will bar regulated crypto firms from handling privacy coins, which limits where it can trade.

outlook.bullCase: Holding above the old $600 resistance could keep momentum going toward the $700 area and, beyond that, the January high near $799.
outlook.bearCase: A leverage flush could drag it back through $600 toward the $520–$560 zone where it bounced earlier this month.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds $600, futures open interest and funding rates, spot volume versus futures volume, and any exchange delisting news.

outlook.bullCase: An official licence filing or Robinhood announcement could push it toward the $4.50–$5 area.

crypto.name: XRP
crypto.move: Down 5.1% in 24h and 2.5% this week, to about $1.31 (down 17% over 30 days)
crypto.why: XRP is drifting lower with the rest of the market after a brief bounce on Wednesday. On the network side, a planned XRP Ledger bug fix was pushed back to November after support from validators (the computers that approve changes) briefly dipped, per a CoinDesk headline. Ripple's push to offer round-the-clock stock trading on crypto rails remains in the news, but no single catalyst explains today's move. CoinDesk notes XRP is trading below its Ichimoku cloud, a chart indicator that some traders read as a sign of building downward momentum.
crypto.meaning: XRP tends to move more than bitcoin in both directions, so it mostly reflects overall risk appetite. The 30-day trend is still down about 14%, and the delayed ledger fix is a minor technical setback rather than a security event.

outlook.bullCase: A broader crypto rally led by bitcoin reclaiming $84,000 could lift XRP back toward the $1.45–$1.50 area.
outlook.bearCase: If bitcoin breaks below $80,000, XRP would likely lose the $1.30 area and could test about $1.20.
outlook.watch: Bitcoin's direction, the rescheduled XRP Ledger fix in November, and U.S. digital-asset rules.

crypto.name: Solana
crypto.move: Down 4.0% in 24h and 2.1% this week, to about $103.50 (down 12% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Solana completed its Alpenglow upgrade, a major overhaul aimed at much faster transaction finality (the point at which a payment can't be reversed), according to CoinDesk. The price has moved with the market rather than rallying on the news, and is down about 4% as altcoins slide.
crypto.meaning: A smooth Alpenglow launch is a meaningful technical milestone, but the market is treating it as already expected. The first days after a big upgrade are when problems usually show up, so stability matters more than headlines.

outlook.bullCase: A trouble-free upgrade and stronger crypto risk appetite could lift SOL back toward $115–$120.

stocks.name: S&P 500
stocks.move: Down about 1.4% at 7,649 Thursday afternoon, near the day's low and about 2.5% below its record near 7,845
stocks.why: The index has kept sliding through the day as Meta, AMD, Amazon and Nvidia fall on renewed doubts about returns from AI spending, while oil near $100 revives inflation worries. Apple (up about 0.8%) and JPMorgan (about flat) are cushioning the drop, the Dow is down only about 0.2%, and the VIX fear gauge is up about 20% to near 20.1.
stocks.meaning: The damage is concentrated in tech, which makes up a large share of the index, while other sectors are holding up better. Falling bond yields help a little, but a 10-year yield near 5% still makes stocks look expensive relative to bonds.

outlook.bullCase: Solid results from Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon next week, a calm Fed on Oct. 28 and yields easing further could carry it back toward the 7,845 record.
outlook.bearCase: A deeper tech sell-off, a hawkish Fed, or an oil spike above $115 could drag it below 7,600 toward the 7,500 area.
outlook.watch: Whether the selling eases into the close, the 7,600 area, oil prices, and the Fed decision on Oct. 28 followed by Microsoft and Alphabet earnings that evening.

stocks.name: Nasdaq Composite
stocks.move: Down about 2.8% at 25,964 Thursday afternoon, near the day's low and about 6% below its 52-week high
stocks.why: Tech is leading the decline: Meta is down about 8.3%, AMD about 8.5%, Amazon about 5.3%, Nvidia about 4.4%, Broadcom about 4% and Alphabet about 3.6%. Chip-equipment makers fell hard after Lam Research's results (down about 9%), and a report about Nvidia and Tesla investing in a Samsung supplier revived worries about AI companies funding their own customers.
stocks.meaning: The AI trade bounced Wednesday, but heavy overnight selling in Asian tech, with Chinese tech shares in Hong Kong having their worst day since April 2025, shows investors are nervous about how much Big Tech is spending on AI and when it pays off.

outlook.bullCase: Upbeat AI revenue and spending commentary from Meta, Microsoft and Alphabet could carry it back toward the 27,500–27,700 highs.
outlook.bearCase: If today's losses extend, the 26,000 level could give way, with the 25,500 area the next stop; disappointing cloud results next week would add pressure.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds 26,000 into the close, the chip-stock losing streak, Alphabet and Microsoft on Oct. 28, and Treasury yields.

stocks.move: Down about 0.9% at 35,986 Thursday afternoon, after closing Wednesday at a four-week high of 36,325
stocks.why: Toronto is following Wall Street lower. stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.move: Down about 8.3% to $640 Thursday afternoon, at the day's low, after closing Wednesday at $697.52
stocks.why: Third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, beating forecasts, and fourth-quarter guidance topped estimates, but the stock is falling as investors focus on costs: Meta expects $135–$145 billion of capital spending, free cash flow was about -$2.1 billion this quarter, and a $9.9 billion legal charge cut reported profit. It also surprised Wall Street with a new non-voting Class C share, one for every share held starting in January 2027; JPMorgan's Doug Anmuth called the pending shares an overhang (a supply worry hanging over the price) and urged Meta to issue any new stock quickly.
stocks.meaning: The core ad business is growing fast, which supports the stock, but AI spending pushed free cash flow negative (about -$2.1 billion) this quarter. A separate $25 billion penalty imposed by a New Mexico judge in a privacy case is under appeal and adds legal uncertainty.

outlook.bullCase: At least 13 brokerages raised price targets after the results, per LSEG; if buyers return to the strong ad growth, it could recover toward the $700 level.
outlook.bearCase: Worry about open-ended AI spending, a share sale to fund it, or the $25 billion New Mexico penalty could push it below today's low near $644 toward the $620–$630 area.
outlook.watch: Whether today's low near $644 holds, any details on Class C share issuance, and Alphabet's and Microsoft's spending plans on Oct. 28.

stocks.meaning: AMD has been one of the biggest AI winners of the past year, more than doubling from its low, so it swings hard when sentiment turns. Its own results on Nov. 3 are the next real test of whether AI chip demand is holding up.

outlook.bearCase: If the AI-spending worry deepens, it could slide toward the $470–$480 area where it traded in late September.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.move: Down about 2.3% to $378 Thursday afternoon, after swinging between about $374 and $389
stocks.why: Tesla rose during the day on Musk's comments that Tesla and SpaceX formed committees to study a merger. After the close it reported adjusted earnings of $0.48 a share versus about $0.45 expected and revenue of $28.05 billion, flat from a year ago and slightly below some forecasts; free cash flow of $1.5 billion beat expectations of a cash burn because spending came in about $3 billion lower than expected. Shares fell about 5% before the open as Tesla cut its 2026 capital-spending plan to about $20 billion from more than $25 billion and Musk said reaching 20,000 Optimus robots a week will take at least a year. Buyers erased the early loss after the open, but the stock has slipped again as the Nasdaq weakened.
stocks.meaning: The core business is weak: operating income fell 56% to $718 million and deliveries slipped 2%, so the stock still trades mostly on robotaxi, Optimus and SpaceX-merger hopes. Lower spending helps cash flow but can read as a slower AI push, which explains the early selling.

outlook.bullCase: Concrete merger progress or a smooth Cybercab expansion to Dallas next month could bring it back toward $400–$410.
outlook.bearCase: If the early dip resumes and analysts trim targets, it could slide back toward $355–$375.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds the $374 area, merger committee news, and the NHTSA Cybercab response due Oct. 30.

stocks.name: Strategy
stocks.move: Down about 5.6% to $145 Thursday afternoon, giving back most of Wednesday's 7.5% gain
stocks.why: Strategy, the largest corporate bitcoin holder with about 848,000 BTC, tends to move two to three times as much as bitcoin.
